criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs builds a squash with a rejected job A, its landed retry B (previous_job = A) and a landed job C that follows B. The gate accepts it. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
criteria.evidence: The new test a_rejected_job_its_landed_retry_and_a_follow_up_land_as_a_chain marks job 0's outcome as Rejected, sets B's base to A's base, and asserts no refusals and that landed_by is CHAIN_IDS[1..]. It passed. The test would fail without the fix: A would stay in closing_jobs and the gate would check it as a chain member.
commands: cargo test -p athena-gate -- rejected fork chain

criteria.criterion: A squash of landed jobs that really fork is still refused with 'both follow'. The existing fork tests pass. Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`.
criteria.evidence: a_forked_chain_is_refused passed. The new a_rejected_job_does_not_hide_a_fork_of_landed_jobs also passed: it checks that two landed retries of one rejected job are refused with 'both follow', and that a plain landed fork (via refused_chain) is too.
commands: cargo test -p athena-gate -- rejected fork chain

criteria.criterion: The code that selects the jobs a commit lands excludes jobs whose recorded outcome is not landed. A doc comment on it says why.
criteria.evidence: closing_jobs in invariant.rs now adds `&& !not_landed(&JobFiles::load(...)?)`. not_landed is true when an outcome is recorded and none of the outcomes (outcome.json or outcome-landed.json) is Landed. The doc comment explains that the job's work never reached the branch and that counting it makes its retry look like a fork. It also says that a job with no outcome record stays in, so the landing check can refuse it.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
criteria.evidence: fmt printed no diffs and clippy finished clean. Every test suite printed 'test result: ok', with 0 failed.

criteria.criterion: docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md or docs/decisions.md records the rule that only landed jobs form the chain.
criteria.evidence: decisions.md adds D74, 'Only landed jobs form a squash's chain', with the decision, alternatives, tradeoff, reversal and provenance. The design doc §4.6 adds a bullet saying the same, and the CHANGELOG has a Fixed entry. Each claim matches the code: the extra head case in chain_problem still checks base_fingerprint against the parent, and a previous job that is absent or has no outcome record still gives 'not linked'.

findings.summary: The exact shape in the report is not tested: a rejected job and its retry both naming the same earlier job as previous_job.
findings.evidence: The error in the request says pf6d and 1r97 'both follow rrf8', so the real retry named rrf8, not pf6d. The fix covers that case too, because the rejected job is dropped from closing_jobs before the followers map is built. But the only new tests set the retry's previous_job to the rejected job, as the criterion asked.

findings.summary: A middle job whose outcome is blocked is no longer tested.
findings.evidence: The old refused_middle case with a Blocked outcome was replaced by a 'no outcome' case. By reading the code, a chain with a blocked middle job is now refused as 'both start a chain', because the next job becomes a second head. No test pins this.

summary: The change does what the request asks. In the gate's landing check, closing_jobs now leaves out any job whose recorded outcome in the commit's tree is not landed, and a doc comment says why. chain_problem now also accepts a chain head whose previous job did not land, as long as the head's base still equals the parent's content. A rejected job whose records ship in a squash therefore no longer makes its retry look like a fork, and no longer makes later jobs look like invalid landings. Landed jobs that fork are still refused with 'both follow'. I ran the new and existing chain tests, the full test suite, clippy and fmt, and all passed. D74, the design doc and the CHANGELOG record the rule accurately. Two minor test gaps: no test uses the exact shape from the report (the retry and the rejected job both following rrf8), which the code still handles, and the blocked-middle-job case is no longer tested. Neither blocks the change.
